reference: No GNU fail2ban-client oracle is available, and the loadables review describes this builtin as a subset rather than a direct CLI drop-in. Contract expectations are independently written from the builtin's documented help/interface contract: Bash type/help metadata, accepted and rejected verbs, the documented IP/jail token rules, and format-status output ordering and missing-database behavior. Expected output bytes are specified here before candidate execution; none were copied from candidate output.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata identifies the builtin and advertises its documented subcommands and read-only control-plane scope.
parse-command accepts the four documented verbs and gives usage status for known unsupported and unknown verbs.
Token validation covers accepted IPv4/IPv6/jail forms, the documented permissive IPv4 digit-width edge, and invalid-token status contracts.
format-status checks sorted unique jail names, file-order IPs including duplicates, malformed-row skipping, and a missing database.
exclusions: No direct GNU fail2ban-client parity case: the pinned loadable review says this is a subset, and no matching client oracle is available.
No daemon, control socket, firewall, network, or live ban/unban/reload operation is run. Those integration behaviors are deferred for a disposable VM with private mocks.

cases.purpose: Check Bash builtin metadata and that help exposes the advertised subcommands and read-only control-plane contract.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t fail2ban) == builtin ]]
doc=$(help fail2ban)
[[ $doc == *'fail2ban selftest'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'parse-command VERB [ARG...]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'format-status DB [JAIL]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'never mutates the db.'* ]]
printf 'metadata contract ok\n'

cases.purpose: Every verb in the documented accepted subset must parse and echo as one line.
cases.script:
for verb in status banip unbanip reload; do
  [[ $(fail2ban parse-command "$verb") == "$verb" ]]
done
printf 'accepted: status banip unbanip reload\n'

cases.purpose: Known out-of-subset verbs and an unknown verb must each return the documented usage status and emit a diagnostic.
cases.script:
for verb in set get bogus; do
  if fail2ban parse-command "$verb"; then
    exit 20
  else
    rc=$?
  fi
  [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]
done
printf 'rejected with usage status\n'

cases.purpose: Accept the documented IPv4 and IPv6 patterns, including a three-digit IPv4 group, and jail names of allowed characters up to the 64-character limit.
cases.script:
fail2ban validate-ip 1.2.3.4
fail2ban validate-ip 12.34.56.789
fail2ban validate-ip fe80::1
fail2ban validate-ip 2001:db8::dead:beef
fail2ban validate-jail sshd
fail2ban validate-jail nginx-http-auth
long_jail=$(printf '%064d' 0)
[[ ${#long_jail} -eq 64 ]]
fail2ban validate-jail "$long_jail"
printf 'valid tokens accepted\n'

cases.purpose: Validator predicates return 1 for false, as in the existing network-smoke regression; status 2 denotes invalid invocation or parse-command tokens.

Format a private database with duplicate jails and malformed/empty fields; jail names must be sorted and unique.
cases.script:
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '2001:db8::1' sshd 1 > ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '198.51.100.4' nginx 2 >> ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '192.0.2.2' sshd 3 >> ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '203.0.113.9' nginx 4 >> ban.db
printf '%s\n' malformed >> ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '' sshd 5 >> ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '192.0.2.99' '' 6 >> ban.db
fail2ban format-status ban.db
cases.stdout:
Status
|- Number of jails:	2
`- Jail list:	nginx sshd

cases.purpose: Filter one jail while retaining database order and duplicate IP entries in the documented status block.
cases.script:
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '203.0.113.8' sshd 1 > ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '198.51.100.1' nginx 2 >> ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '203.0.113.8' sshd 3 >> ban.db
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' '2001:db8::2' sshd 4 >> ban.db
printf '%s\n' malformed >> ban.db
fail2ban format-status ban.db sshd
cases.stdout:
Status for the jail: sshd
|- Currently banned:	3
`- Banned IP list:	203.0.113.8 203.0.113.8 2001:db8::2

cases.purpose: Exercise actual banip/unbanip policy changes and backend effects through the integration layer.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM containing the fail2ban-client wrapper, an isolated temporary ban database, and an injectable fake firewall actor. Verify ban/unban state transitions and that calls are confined to the mock; this loadable only parses the verbs and owns no firewall or database mutation path.

cases.purpose: Exercise reload and daemon-backed status behavior across the client control interface.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a disposable fail2ban-compatible daemon and private Unix control socket, plus a mocked firewall backend. The loadable does not open a daemon socket or implement daemon reload/status operations, so metadata and parser checks cannot establish this integration behavior.
